text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.
WHEAT TENDERS - The CCC on Sept 10 seeks 19,860 tonnes of soft white wheat of which 15,340 is for donation to Ethiopia and 4,520 for Pakistan. Shipment is for Sept 25-Oct 20.
BARLEY TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission said it invited offers September 3 to supply 25,000 tonnes of feed barley, with shipment for Sept 25-Oct 10 from Europe or Sept 15-30 from North America.

SOYBEAN TENDER - South Korea said it will tender Sept 5 for 20,000 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 soybeans. Bids will be opened Sept 6. He said shipment was set for Sept 26-Oct 15 if from the U.S. Gulf or for October 11-30 if from the Pacific Northwest. Arrival was set for the western port city of Inchon by November 20.

CORN AND SOYBEAN TENDER - State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp will tender on Thursday for 20,000 tonnes of No.2 or better U.S. yellow corn and 10,000 tonnes of No.2 or better U.S. yellow soybeans, traders said. A Taiwan Sugar buyer, who confirmed the tender plan, said the Iraq crisis already was driving international grain prices higher and that Thursday's tender was the soonest Taiwan Sugar could arrange. The maximun moisture limits for the shipment are specified at 14.5 percent for the corn and 13.5 percent for the soybeans.

VEGOIL TENDER - Tunisia will tender on Wednesday for the purchase of up to 122,000 tonnes of soy and/or rapeseed oils for October/November delivery, the state-buying body Office National de l'Huile said. It said the tender was for one or two lots of 3,000 or 6,000 tonnes to be delivered on October 5-20 and November 5-20.

MARKET TALK - Russia on Tuesday revised upwards the amount of corn and soymeal it plans to buy this year from the West to 4.0 to 4.5 million tonnes and said downpours in Siberia could affect the total grain harvest.
Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun told an industry meeting in St. Petersburg that Moscow would buy corn and soymeal from the United States, Canada and Australia this year.

MARKET TALK cont'd - Several U.S. exporters said they had seen no evidence yet of Russian interest in major purchases of U.S. grain and soymeal. "There are occasions when we hear from them and they nibble for 20,000 or 80,000 tons of corn or meal. But it never happens because they end up buying from some eastern European country where they rail it in," one exporter said on condition he not be named.
... The renewed hostilities in Iraq that suspended its oil-for-food agreement with the U.N. will depress declining world wheat prices, European grain traders said.
... India has so far signed export deals for 200,000 tonnes of soymeal for November-December shipments, traders said.
